title: growth-contrasts-scratch
content:
Purpose: quick, messy scratchpad for my midyear sync and self-review prep. Keep this short and portable — copy bits into the formal review doc later.

Context notes (two-line summaries):
- Role focus: enable engineering org growth by improving onboarding, leveling clarity, and manager enablement.
- Past quarter: launched new onboarding checklist pilot (pilot cohort = 12 hires), started manager office hours; still iterating on feedback loop.

Top objectives (what success looks like by end of Q3):
1) Onboarding quality: reduce new-hire time-to-first-impact from ~6w to <=4w for ICs in engineering.
   - Success signals: first PR merged within 3 weeks for 70% of cohort; survey NPS >= +25 at 30 days.
2) Manager enablement: standardized 1:1 framework + manager onboarding playbook adopted by 85% of new managers.
   - Success signals: 1:1 template used in >80% of new-manager 1:1s (tracked via forms), reduce manager ramp tickets by 40%.
3) Calibration hygiene: create lightweight promotion rubric and pilot with 2 teams.
   - Success signals: rubric used in 2 promotion cycles; managers report rubric reduced calibration time by 30%.

Evidence bank (quick bullets to cite in review):
- Onboarding pilot metrics (internal sheet): cohort size 12; mean time-to-first-PR = 28 days; median = 24 days.
- Survey snippets: "first week orientation was crisp" (EngE1), "still unclear where to find infra docs" (EngE3).
- Manager office hours: 6 sessions, avg attendance 8, recurring asks: career convo structure, how to give corrective feedback.
- Promotion rubric draft: v0.2 in GH PR #58; feedback from Platform ENG and SRE.

Stories that matter (narratives I want manager to remember):
- The onboarding playbook fixed a consistent early experience: Sam from infra shipped infra/docs updates that stopped 3 repeated blockers for new hires.
- Manager office hours once surfaced a recurring gap: managers were uncomfortable running calibration discussions; from that we turned one session into an actionable script and paired managers for practice.

Manager sync agenda (15 min, compact):
1) Quick wins (60s): onboarding pilot improved median PR time to 24d.
2) Ask (90s): short-term resource ask — can we allocate 0.1 FTE of eng-docs support for 6 weeks to fix infra doc gaps? (impact: accelerates onboarding metric by estimated 10–15%).
3) Risk (60s): promotion rubric still needs 2 cross-team reviews; if delayed, promotion cycle will be messy in Sept.
4) Decision/commit (60s): agree owner for doc support and confirm reviewers for rubric.

Open questions I want to raise with manager (bulleted):
- Tradeoff: prioritize onboarding docs vs. running more manager practice sessions? Which has higher ROI given hiring plan?
- If we get a headcount adjustment in mid-July, do we reserve for a 0.5 FTE contractor or keep flexibility?
- Is the style of the rubric (behavioral anchors + examples) acceptable for exec-level sign-off or do we need a condensed one-pager?

Risks & mitigations (short):
- Risk: Documentation fixes require eng time and deprioritization could stall onboarding improvements.
  Mitigation: propose docs squad with 0.1 eng-docs allocation and prioritize top 10 blockers from survey.
- Risk: Managers don't adopt 1:1 framework.
  Mitigation: pilot with incentives (peer recognition + small manager cohort coaching).

Micro-experiments (what to try next 6 weeks):
- A/B test: replace week-1 mentor check-in with a structured "day 5 demo" prompt and measure PR velocity.
- Quick doc sprint: 3-day hackweek with two engineers + one content writer to fix top infra docs.
- Coaching bundle: 4-session manager micro-cohort (90m sessions) and peer shadowing.

Action checklist (copy to task list):
- [ ] Draft 1:1 template final copy (due 2025-07-01) — owner: me.
- [ ] Submit resource ask for 0.1 eng-docs (prepare cost estimate) — owner: me.
- [ ] Request rubric reviewers (Platform ENG, SRE lead) — owner: me.
- [ ] Run A/B for day-5 demo with next hiring batch (start 2025-07-15).

Tiny rehearsals (soundbites for manager):
- "Short ask: 0.1 FTE for 6 weeks; payoff = ~10% faster time-to-first-impact for new hires." 
- "We can de-risk promotions with a lightweight rubric in two teams this cycle."

Notes to future self (handy reminders):
- Keep this doc focused on measurable things — use numbers not platitudes.
- When pasting into the review, trim anecdotes to 1–2 sentences max.
- Save a copy titled 'final-review-snippet' once I move bullet metrics.

End-of-scratch: prune before formal review; share with Evan for a sanity check 24h before sync.
